title: Phở Gà Nguyệt (chicken phở)
why: Michelin Bib Gourmand 2026; broth starts simmering at 4am from pork and chicken bones that are never reused.

title: Bún Chả Đắc Kim (bún chả)
why: Michelin Selected 2026; smoky grilled pork belly and patties, nước chấm sharpened with pickled green mango. 1 Hàng Mành St.

title: Miến Lươn Chân Cầm (eel vermicelli)
why: Michelin Bib Gourmand; ~40 years on one dish, eels from Bắc Ninh fried without batter, cassava noodles from Cự Đà. 1 Chân Cầm St.

title: Chả Cá Thăng Long (turmeric grilled catfish)
why: Michelin Bib Gourmand; grilled at your table in a sizzling pan with dill and spring onion. Three same-named outlets on one street - go to 6B Dương Thành St.

title: Phở Bò Ấu Triệu (beef phở, one dish only)
why: Michelin Bib Gourmand; no signage, a single dish, a 10-hour beef bone broth with flank and tendon. 34 Ấu Triệu.

title: Bún Chả Ta (bún chả + crab spring rolls)
why: Michelin Bib Gourmand; several spring-roll variants, the seafood-crab one is the pick. 21 Nguyễn Hữu Huân St.

title: Xới Cơm (Northern Vietnamese home cooking)
why: Michelin Bib Gourmand; daily-changing menu, 1980s Hanoi interior, staff explain the menu in simple English. Good for a proper sit-down meal. 107 Lane 36 Láng Hạ St.

title: Don Duck Old Quarter
why: Michelin Bib Gourmand; duck every conceivable way - duck phở, Peking-style grilled duck, hotpot, spring rolls. 29 Bát Đàn St.

title: Hiệu Lực Canh Cá Rô Hưng Yên (perch fish noodles)
why: Michelin Selected 2026; two kinds of noodle in one bowl under crispy deep-fried perch and fish cakes. Order the đặc biệt. 39 Hai Bà Trưng St.

title: Egg coffee (cà phê trứng)
why: Hanoi's own invention - whipped egg yolk over strong coffee with condensed milk. Giang Café on Hàng Gai is the most-cited original (cramped, cash-only). Identical drink at 25k or 80k VND; you pay for the room.

title: Habakuk (specialty coffee by day, bistro by night)
why: Michelin Bib Gourmand; single-origin coffee and brunch by day, modern Mediterranean-ish bistro in the evening. 4 Phan Huy Chú Lane - look for the blue back-lit signs.

title: Bia hoi (fresh draught beer) at the Old Quarter beer corner
why: Cheaper than bottled water and the social centre of Hanoi evenings, around Tạ Hiện. 10,000-15,000 VND a glass per the 2026 Bia Hoi Index.

title: Hanoi Train Street (from inside a café)
why: The alley where a mainline train passes inches from the cafés. You cannot just walk in - police block entrances and since 25 Mar tourists may not freely enter the trackside cafés. Working method: sit in a café as a paying customer, check the day's train times locally, have a backup plan.

title: Long Biên Bridge at sunset
why: Rusted century-old cantilever bridge; the mid-span walkway at golden hour is the classic Hanoi photograph and it is free.

title: Hoàn Kiếm Lake at dusk + Ngọc Sơn temple
why: The heart of the city: Turtle Tower, the red Húc Bridge, and the evening crowd. Free to walk; the temple on the island has an entrance fee (could not confirm).

title: Hỏa Lò Prison (the 'Hanoi Hilton')
why: Colonial prison turned museum; the most affecting history stop in Hanoi. Sources conflict on the ticket (30,000 vs 50,000 VND) - the night tour is a separate ticket.

title: Old Quarter street-food crawl + Đồng Xuân market early
why: The market runs 5-9am for fresh phở beef and bánh mì stops; the Old Quarter's internal alleys (Hàng Gà, Hàng Mành) are 40-50% cheaper than the lakeside tourist zone for the same dish.

title: Hai Bà Trưng lunch (the underrated food street)
why: Locals eat here, tourists have not discovered it - fewer stalls, less crowding, strong bún chả and rice bowls. Near Hàng Trọng Street.

title: New Year's Eve fireworks at Hoàn Kiếm Lake
why: Midnight fireworks over the lake with stages near the Opera House and at Thống Nhất Park; thousands gather from the Húc Bridge area. The reason to route the trip so NYE lands in Hanoi.

title: Peridot Grand Hotel & Spa
why: Best mid-range value in the Old Quarter (guide-quoted US$75-110/night) - modern 2022 interior, rooftop bar, central. See data/accommodation.json acc-003 for the full entry.

title: Hanoi La Siesta Premium Hang Be
why: The splurge (guide-quoted US$90-130/night): quiet inner courtyard 300m from Hoan Kiem Lake, own spa, consistently among the city's highest-rated. Also the pick for the single NYE night.

title: Trang An boat trip
why: UNESCO World Heritage; a 2.5-3 hour rowboat through limestone river caves and riverside temples, three route options. The longer, better boat than Tam Coc.

title: Hang Mua (Mua Cave) sunrise viewpoint
why: ~500 stone steps to the dragon-statue viewpoint over Tam Coc. The single best photograph in Ninh Binh. Go at sunrise - the tour buses arrive from Hanoi at 9-10am and boats start at 7-8am, so you have a two-hour window.

title: Tam Coc boat trip
why: Foot-paddled rowboat through three caves past rice paddies, ~1.5-2 hours. Shorter and busier than Trang An; rowers expect a tip on top of the ticket.

title: Cycle the Tam Coc back lanes to Bích Động and Thái Vi
why: The underrated Ninh Binh. Most people do the day-trip-from-Hanoi version and never see this. Bicycles are ~50,000 VND/day from most Tam Coc homestays.

title: Thịt dê (mountain goat) in Ninh Binh
why: The region's signature dish - grilled, stir-fried or in a hotpot. Restaurants cluster around Tam Coc, Trang An and Ninh Binh city. Father Cooking Restaurant in Tam Coc is the most-reviewed specific venue I could source.

title: Father Cooking Restaurant
why: ~796 TripAdvisor reviews, consistently named for goat meat. In the Tam Coc area (Ninh Hải, Hoa Lư).

title: Tam Coc Garden Resort
why: Best all-round mid-range pick for the Ninh Binh leg (guide-quoted US$35-55/night): bungalows in a genuine garden with an unobstructed view of the Mua Cave karst range, pool, 15 min walk to the pier. See acc-010.

title: Ha Giang loop - 4 days / 3 nights with an easy rider
why: The centrepiece of the trip and the only legal way for a Singapore licence holder to do it (Vietnam does not recognise AA Singapore's 1949-convention IDP). A local licensed driver takes you pillion through Quan Ba, Yen Minh, Dong Van, Ma Pi Leng and Du Gia. All-inclusive: bike, driver, fuel, border permit, homestays, meals, boat ticket.

title: Mã Pì Lèng Pass
why: The highlight of the whole trip: ~20km of road cut into a cliff above the Nho Quế river gorge, between Đồng Văn and Mèo Vạc. The single best ride and the single best photograph on the loop.

title: Nho Quế river boat trip (below Mã Pì Lèng)
why: A boat down the gorge you were just looking down into. Usually included in easy-rider tour prices.

title: Quản Bạ 'Heaven's Gate' (Cổng trời Quản Bạ)
why: The twin-mountains viewpoint at the top of the first big climb out of Ha Giang city - the loop's opening statement and the natural first photo stop.

title: Đồng Văn old town + Sunday market
why: Old H'Mong houses, the H'Mong King's Palace nearby, and the plateau's main market. The Sunday market is the set-piece: livestock, textiles, thắng cố, and the social hub of the plateau. Timing is weekly - check which village's market falls on your day before fixing the departure.

title: Lũng Cú flag tower + Lô Lô Chải village
why: Vietnam's northernmost point, a landmark tower with a view over the Chinese border, and the H'Mong village of Lô Lô Chải at its foot. Note the whole area is inside the border-permit zone.
cost_estimate: small entrance fee, could not confirm

title: Dữ Già village + waterfalls (the reason for a 4-day loop)
why: The quiet southern leg - waterfall swims, a village homestay, and none of the convoy traffic. This is what you gain by doing 4 days/3 nights instead of 3 days/2 nights.

title: Thắng cố (thang co) - the H'Mong market stew
why: The plateau's signature dish, traditionally horse meat simmered with herbs and offal, now often beef or buffalo. An acquired taste and a genuine cultural set-piece - eat it at a market, not a restaurant.

title: Cháo ấu tẩu (au tau porridge) - the underrated one
why: Rice porridge made with a rare, slightly bitter mountain root, sold as a warming breakfast on cold mornings. Cheap, and almost no visitor orders it because the name is unpronounceable. Perfect for a fogged-in December pass morning.

title: Bánh tam giác mạch (buckwheat cake)
why: The plateau's buckwheat griddle cake - the edible symbol of the region. Note the buckwheat *flowers* peak Oct-Nov, so in late December you get the cake, not the pink fields.

title: Village homestay dinner on the loop (cơm lam, five-colour sticky rice, smoked buffalo)
why: Family-style dinner at a H'Mong or Dao stilt-house, usually included in the tour price. This is the meal, rather than any restaurant. Tell your operator about dietary requirements before you leave, not on the mountain - vegetarian food is genuinely hard on the loop.
cost_estimate: included in the tour; standalone homestays 100,000-200,000 VND incl. dinner + breakfast

title: Yen Bien Luxury Hotel (Ha Giang city)
why: The post-loop reset night: 4-star, rooftop pool, mountain views, 5 minutes' walk from the Km 0 milestone. Note the two sources disagree on price (1,065,000 VND vs US$25) - verify. See acc-015.

title: Lo Lo Eco Lodge (Lô Lô Chải, Đồng Văn)
why: Closest stay to the Lũng Cú flag tower; dorm from ~US$8, earthen family rooms ~US$17, wooden bungalow with balcony ~US$25. On a bookable tour the operator assigns loop accommodation, so confirm rather than assume.

title: Hanoi -> Ha Giang by daytime limousine van
why: 6-7 hours door-to-door vs 7-8 by sleeper bus, and you get the mountain road in daylight. Hotel pickup in the Old Quarter. Recommended over the overnight bus for this trip. Operators: Bang Phan, Ngoc Cuong VIP, Quang Nghi, Cat Ba Express.

title: Hanoi -> Ninh Binh by limousine van (or train)
why: 2-2.5 hours. The limousine van (200,000-350,000 VND) gives Old Quarter hotel pickup and drops in Tam Coc. The train is the cheapest once you add taxi costs both ends and is the prettier ride.
cost_estimate: 200,000-350,000 VND van; 95,000-150,000 VND train soft seat

title: Noi Bai airport -> Old Quarter by Bus 86
why: The cheapest sane airport transfer, and it passes Hoan Kiem Lake and the Opera House on the way to the railway station. Runs ~07:00-22:05, ~50-55 minutes. Carry small notes - the airport's own notice says 50,000 VND, most travel sites say 45,000.

title: Grab / Xanh SM for the Noi Bai transfer
why: Fixed in-app price removes meter risk. Watch out: since 3 Aug 2026 ride-hailing cars cannot pick up at the terminal kerb - T1 to car park P2, T2 (international) to P1, peak times possibly P7. That is a walk with luggage.

title: Ha Giang border-area entry permit
why: Foreigners have long needed permission for the land-border districts that the loop runs through (Quan Ba, Yen Minh, Dong Van, Meo Vac). From 1 June 2026 some operators advise a new Border Area Entry Permit (~US$10) is checked at active checkpoints, but Time Out could find no official government notice - treat it as operator guidance, not confirmed law. Ask your operator IN WRITING whether it is included, and carry your passport and cash.

title: Do NOT self-ride a motorbike in Vietnam on a Singapore licence
why: Vietnam recognises only 1968 Vienna Convention IDPs, used with the matching national licence. AA Singapore issues IDPs under the 1949 Geneva Convention and states on its own site that Vietnam does not recognise them. So a Singapore licence + IDP does not legally cover a >50cc bike, and travel insurance will very likely not pay out after a crash. This is the brief's 'real trap', and the answer is: book an easy rider instead.

title: No visa needed - Singapore passport holders get 30 days visa-free
why: Vietnam's own government portal lists Singapore ordinary passports under a bilateral visa-exemption agreement; Singapore MFA puts the stay at up to 30 days per entry. Do not buy an e-visa or an 'approval letter'. Condition: passport valid at least 6 months, plus a return/onward ticket.

title: Book Christmas and NYE Hanoi hotels first
why: 24, 25 and 31 December in Hanoi is the tightest accommodation window of the Vietnamese year - the Old Quarter's good mid-range sells out and prices 30-50% above low season. This is the single most time-critical booking on the trip. Book within 2-4 weeks.

title: Japanese encephalitis + rabies - ask the doctor before you go
why: CDC recommends Hep A, Hep B and typhoid for Vietnam, and says to CONSIDER Japanese encephalitis and rabies for short-term travellers doing rural/hiking/outdoor activities or staying without screens - which is exactly the Ha Giang loop. Multi-dose series, so book the appointment 6+ weeks out.
